events.label: Construction
events.description: The Hôtel de Sens was built on the order of Tristan de Salazar, archbishop of Sens.

events.label: Marguerite de Valois
events.description: Marguerite de Valois, known as Queen Margot, occupied the house for a short period. The Ville de Paris page describes the stay as lasting several months; the year range comes from the Musée Carnavalet object history.

events.label: Private rentals
events.description: The archbishops left in 1622. The building was rented to private occupants until the Revolution.

events.label: Commercial and industrial uses
events.description: After sale as national property, successive occupants used the building for transport, laundry, food production, hare-hair cutting, jam making, and glass storage.

events.label: Thomas Shotter Boys lithograph
events.description: A published lithograph records the corner turret and a busy street scene. It is an authored print, not a photograph.

events.label: Saint James jam works photographed
events.description: Pierre Emonts or Emonds photographed the street façade with the Confiturerie de Saint James sign over the entrance on April 27, 1869.

events.label: Eugène Atget photograph
events.description: Atget photographed a corner turret and the tightly adjoining street fabric.

events.label: Municipal acquisition
events.description: The City of Paris bought the building in a state described by the city as extremely dilapidated.

events.label: Historic-monument classification order
events.description: The current Ministry of Culture record lists a classification order dated March 20, 1912.

events.label: Agence Meurisse before frame
events.description: The supplied photograph matches Agence Meurisse image 80722, dated May 26, 1920, in the Bibliothèque nationale de France.

events.label: Demolition opposite the hotel
events.description: Gustave Ferdinand Boberg made a drawing explicitly titled as demolition of old houses opposite the Hôtel de Sens.

events.label: Restoration
events.description: The municipal restoration began in 1929 and ended in 1961. The sources reviewed for this package do not provide an element-by-element inventory of replaced and retained fabric.

events.label: Bibliothèque Forney transfer
events.description: Paris adopted the transfer plan in 1929. The collections began moving 32 years later, in 1961.

events.label: Modern after frame
events.description: Guilhem Vellut photographed the restored street façade on August 28, 2016.
